quality-1-light.note: Stop 1 of the five-stop measured-signal-quality ramp (bad, hue 27). THE RAMP IS A LIGHTNESS STAIRCASE, NOT A HUE WHEEL: under deuteranopia hues 27/45/72/115/149 flatten onto one yellow axis, so each ramp is monotone in lightness (light 0.385 -> 0.505 in 0.030 steps; dark 0.640 -> 0.800 in 0.045 steps) and BAR LENGTH carries adjacent distinctions. Adjacent stops sit BELOW the 0.05 CVD separation floor deliberately; every non-adjacent pair clears it (worst 0.055 light, 0.077 dark). Do not 'fix' this to satisfy a contrast rule — the fix would destroy the scale. `--quality-N` is the NUMERAL ink; `--quality-N-bar` is the BAR fill, one lightness step bolder. In light, stops 1-3 resolve to deep reds and browns because 4.5:1 on a near-white ground caps those hues at L ~ 0.50 — a gamut ceiling, not a conservative choice.

quality-1-dark.note: Dark-theme value of `quality-1`. The dark ramp is genuinely vivid where the light one cannot be; the staircase runs 0.640 -> 0.800 in 0.045 steps.

quality-1-bar-light.note: The BAR fill for stop 1, one lightness step bolder than `--quality-1` because a 4px fill needs more weight than a text figure to read as the same colour. Reached through `MetricBar`'s static `TONE_CLASS` (`quality-1` -> `bg-quality-1-bar`); a ramp tone on a fill whose LENGTH does not encode the value is a bug, and so is ramp ink on a numeral with no bar beside it.

chart-6-light.note: Legacy token retained only for signal-storm-game.tsx. Retargeted onto quality stop 2's bar value. The whole `--chart-1..6` block is deletable once this and `--chart-3` move to `--chart-nr` / a quality stop.

chart-6-dark.note: Dark-theme value of `chart-6`. Authored, not derived by inversion — both themes are first-class and every value in both was measured.

display.purpose: 700 / 1.875rem (30px) / -0.02em. The h1 at the top of every feature page, followed by an `on-surface-variant` description. One per route.

headline.purpose: 600 / 1.25rem (20px) / -0.01em. Large tile values, state-screen labels, section headings inside a hero card.

title.purpose: 600 / 1.125rem (18px). The card title. `CardTitle` itself ships only `leading-none font-semibold` and takes its size from the call site.

body.purpose: 400 / 0.875rem (14px). Descriptions, prose, card copy, table cells. `leading-relaxed` and `text-pretty` on any paragraph over one line.

row.purpose: 600 / 0.8125rem (13px) on an explicit 20px line box. The leading is not optional: 13px is an arbitrary Tailwind size, so the pinned line box is what holds the row at exactly 40px and keeps its skeleton's `h-10` a real mirror. Never reach for 13px outside a dense metric row.

label.purpose: 500 / 0.75rem (12px). Chips, tags, table headers, button text, form labels, tile eyebrows. Sidebar section labels run 11px with `tracking-wider`.

numeric.purpose: 600 with `tabular-nums`, in `--font-sans` rather than mono. The one step deliberately NOT on a fixed ramp: a numeral is read at the distance its container implies, so its size derives from the slot holding it and a literal `text-[Npx]` is correct by construction here.

banner.purpose: 600 / 15px with `tracking-[-0.005em]`, description 13px. 15px is the only sanctioned literal outside the pre-auth scale: a banner title must out-weigh the copy beneath it without competing with the card heading above it, on a surface that mounts at any width on any route.

preAuth.purpose: A denser five-step scale of its own: card title 600/19px/-0.01em, section title 600/17px, emphasis 600/15px, body 400-600/13px, eyebrow 600/11px `tracking-[0.11em]` uppercase. These are the only two screens that are a single card on an empty canvas, so they build five levels of hierarchy from nothing inside ~400px. Both surfaces change together in one commit.

mono.purpose: JetBrains Mono, self-hosted at build time. Identifiers (band, EARFCN, PCI, ICCID, IMEI, MAC/IP), static facts read back from config, raw AT responses, log lines, copyable commands. The tell: does the value change while the user watches without them acting? Then `font-sans` with `tabular-nums`. Does it hold steady until something reconfigures it? Then `font-mono`. A human-authored label never wears it.

shadows.name: whisper
shadows.purpose: Optional card lift in light mode. Resolves to `0 0 #0000` in dark, where a shadow is invisible against a near-black ground and the tonal step does the work. Never load-bearing. Light's canvas-to-card step is 0.985 -> 1.000, deliberately narrow, and the whisper is what keeps that edge legible without reaching for a hairline.

shadows.name: popover-float
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, dropdowns, popovers, the skip-to-content pill. The 'not part of the page flow' signal, and the one place a shadow carries real meaning.

motion.name: ease-emphasized
motion.purpose: A deliberate departure and a long settle. Container size and shape, aggregation re-proportioning, banner arrival, meter first-fill. Mirrored in lib/motion.ts as `EASE_EMPHASIZED`.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The everyday state change, and the right default. Card entrance, nav indicator, chip morph, meter retarget. Mirrored as `EASE_STANDARD`.

motion.name: ease-quick
motion.purpose: Moves too brief to need shaping: label swaps, value ticks, hover tints, focus rings. At the short end of the scale a bespoke cubic is indistinguishable from the built-in. These two curves plus `ease-out` are the WHOLE vocabulary — an `ease-[cubic-bezier(...)]` arbitrary value is a violation, not a variant.

motion.name: ease-ambient
motion.purpose: The two sanctioned ambient loops only, paired with `alternate` (the live-ping does not alternate: a radar sweep only travels outward).

motion.name: duration-quick
motion.purpose: Label swaps, live value ticks, hover tints, focus rings — and the exit clock for every modal surface, content and scrim alike. That second job is load-bearing: Radix pins `pointer-events: none` on `<body>` until the exit animation ends, so this number is literally how long the page ignores clicks after a dialog closes.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: The default for a state change: card entrance, nav indicator, chip fill+ink morph, meter retarget.

motion.name: duration-emphasized
motion.purpose: Container size and shape, aggregation re-proportioning, banner arrival, meter first-fill, modal open. This is the ceiling for the whole product — state the rule as the token, never as the number.

motion.name: duration-ambient
motion.purpose: The service-ring pulse and the live-ping dot. Nothing else loops. Deliberately NOT doubled with the transition tokens: a loop is not a transition, and at 4s a breathing ring reads as a stalled UI rather than a calm one.

motion.name: stagger-step
motion.purpose: The card cascade step, with a 10px rise (`staggerContainer` / `staggerItem`). Wider and the last card reads as the page still loading. Also drives the CA meter column's arrival cascade via `--meter-index`.

motion.name: stagger-step-rows
motion.purpose: The in-card row cascade, with a 5px rise (`staggerRows` / `staggerRowItem`). Rows sit ~6px apart, so a 10px lift would move each row past its neighbour's resting position and read as the card reflowing. JS-only (`STAGGER_STEP_ROWS`); `rowCascadeDelay(index)` derives both this step and its ten-row cap from it.

motion.name: tick-stagger-step
motion.purpose: The step between two figures' dips inside one `TickGroup`, by live DOM position rather than map index. Not an entrance, which is why it does not violate the two-stagger-step rule: nothing is arriving. Floor is ~1/8th of the dip, below which consecutive dips merge.

motion.name: tick
motion.purpose: The live value tick: asymmetric on purpose — the dip is the event, the return is the settle. The tightest thing in the system against the poll: a seven-figure cascade runs 1.4s of lead plus a 1.4s dip against a measured ~3.7-4.0s poll cadence, leaving ~900ms. Re-check that arithmetic before raising the scale or speeding up the poller. Only measurements tick; identifiers take the container morph instead.

motion.name: save-check-overshoot
motion.purpose: The one sanctioned overshoot in the entire product, exported as a NUMBER (`SAVE_CHECK_OVERSHOOT` / `SAVE_CHECK_KEYFRAMES` / `transitionSaveCheck`) rather than promised in prose. Keyframes, not a spring: the peak is the constant, not an emergent property of two dial settings. A ceiling enforced only by prose is not a ceiling.

breakpoints.name: @4xl/main

breakpoints.name: @5xl/main

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: The one named viewport breakpoint (`--breakpoint-desktop`), for shell-level concerns. Viewport breakpoints otherwise stay for the page gutter (`px-4 lg:px-6`) and the sidebar's own collapse.

radii.name: rounded-field

radii.name: rounded-tile

radii.name: rounded-card
radii.purpose: 36px: standard cards in a grid, dialogs.

radii.name: rounded-hero

radii.name: rounded-pill
radii.purpose: Chips, tags, buttons, nav items, metric rows, meters, glyph discs, quality bars.

radii.name: --radius (legacy)
radii.purpose: The legacy `rounded-{sm,md,lg,xl}` chain still resolves for unconverted call sites and keeps its old values — including inside the shadcn primitives themselves (`Button` is `rounded-md h-9`, `Card` is `rounded-xl border shadow-sm`). iconLibraries.name: Material Symbols Rounded
iconLibraries.scope: The sidebar, /dashboard, the two pre-auth routes (/ and /login/), and the entire /cellular/ family — index plus all 17 sub-routes.
iconLibraries.note: Ligature-driven and self-hosted, subset at build time from a shared glyph list, so `font-feature-settings: 'liga'` is what makes an icon an icon. Sets `fontSize` as an inline style, which outranks any utility — a parent's `[&>svg]:size-3` cannot reach it, so pass `size` explicitly at every call site (12 in a dense chip, 16 where the glyph carries quality). Always `aria-hidden` beside a real text label. Its `FILL` axis is animatable and the active nav row thickens it 0 -> 1, which is what makes the active state survive grayscale.

iconLibraries.name: lucide-react
iconLibraries.scope: Every other route — /local-network/, /monitoring/, /system-settings/, /about-device, /support, onboarding — plus every route-agnostic primitive (the page-level `Banner`, the apply-progress dialog) wherever it mounts.
iconLibraries.note: The boundary is per ROUTE, never per directory. A lucide glyph on an unconverted route is correct code, not a defect, and a route-agnostic component stays on lucide even when it mounts inside a Material route, because it cannot know where it will appear. Convert a whole route or none of it.

iconLibraries.scope: The dashboard Network Status card only.

components.description: The only correct status indicator, and one of exactly two chip forms. A role container, that container's ink, no visible border, pill radius, and a mandatory 12px glyph. The glyph is load-bearing — `success-container` and `warning-container` have measured 1.03:1 apart. Fill and ink run on `standard`, the focus ring on `quick`. Hover is `[a&]:`-scoped so a static chip never advertises a click target that does not exist.

components.name: Outline Tag
components.description: The second chip form, and the split is the point: a filled chip says whether a thing is WELL, an outline tag says what a thing IS — a band number, a radio family, a channel width, a capability. Four variants: `nr`, `lte`, `spatial`, `neutral`. Geometry mirrors `Badge` exactly so the two forms sit on one baseline when a surface renders both; what differs is the fill (none) and the border (visible, role-coloured). No glyph requirement, because there is no second state for a glyph to disambiguate. Text and border are separate tokens because they clear different thresholds (4.5:1 vs 3:1), so `border-current` would fail one of them. This replaced the filled identity chip: `nr` / `lte` / `spatial` / `downlink` / `uplink` were DELETED from `badge.tsx`, so `variant="nr"` on a Badge now fails the build.

components.name: Quality Bar
components.description: The row-level data graphic and the non-chromatic half of the quality ramp. A full-round `surface-container` track 4px tall, spanning the row where the row is the bar's own line and shrinking to a 56px lane where it sits inline beside its figure. The fill is `--quality-N-bar` and its LENGTH is proportional to the value within the metric's physical range — length is the primary encoding and colour only reinforces it, which is what makes adjacent ramp stops safe below the separation floor. A missing reading renders an EMPTY TRACK with no fill element at all (`MetricBar value={null}`), never a zero-length red fill. The entrance is a compositor-only `scaleX` on mount; the value retarget is layout `width`, because a transform scales the border-radius too and squashed the pill cap into an ellipse at low percentages.

components.name: Hero Card
components.description: The anchor card on a surface: 40px radius, `border-0` explicit, `surface` fill, 28px horizontal padding, tonal separation only, with an optional whisper shadow that is never load-bearing. A grid of peer cards takes `rounded-card` (36px) and 24px padding instead. The header is plain `CardTitle` plus `CardDescription` — never an icon in a card header.

THE BODY IS NEUTRAL AND THE DISC CARRIES THE COLOUR — the previous four-tinted-tile strip encoded category without encoding importance, so it flattened to equal weight with nowhere for the eye to land; a neutral body with a saturated disc gives the tile a focal point at 1/8th the tinted area. The disc uses the role's strong FILL, never the pale container. The height is pinned rather than floored because a floor cannot be a mirror: live tiles measured 118 / 98 / 95px against a 92px skeleton.

components.description: The glance-surface metric row: a 40px full-round pill on `surface-container`, 16px horizontal, a 13px/600 `on-surface-variant` key against a 13px value. No dividers. The 20px line box is load-bearing — it holds the row at exactly 40px so its skeleton's `h-10` keeps mirroring it. The value is `font-mono` when it is an identifier and `font-sans tabular-nums` when it is a live measurement; A VALUE THAT CARRIES QUALITY TAKES ITS RAMP INK HERE, and then it must have a bar beside it and an `sr-only` quality word. First paint is non-animated (`data-settling`) so the pill starts under the active row instead of sliding up from zero.

narrative.northStar: An instrument console — colour on the data, not on the furniture.
narrative.overview:
QManager reports what a cellular modem is doing, on the modem itself, to someone who understands modems. Three facts about that job set the whole language.

**Colour belongs to the data, not to the furniture.** A card is a neutral surface. What is coloured is the reading: the numeral, the chart stroke, the quality bar, the glyph in its disc. This is the largest change from the previous system, which spent its colour on large tonal container fills and left the live diagnostic values grey — on the very surface built to showcase the palette, four tinted tiles carried restated facts while RSRP and SINR sat in neutral text below them.

It is also the accessible answer, which is not a coincidence. Across this palette, ink colours separate in 0 of 28 pairs under deuteranopia and protanopia simulation, and so do fills, while pale identity containers collapse in 8 of 10. Colour on ink works; colour on large pale surfaces does not, and an optimiser proved the light-mode pale band too narrow to hold five identity hues plus `surface-container-high` — infeasible, not merely hard. So the system commits to the layer that survives: identity gets ink, an outline, and a strong-fill disc, and never a large tinted block.

**Density is the product, and hierarchy is how it stays readable.** A modem console shows a lot at once. The answer is never to show less; it is to rank what is shown. Neutral surfaces, one coloured thing per row, and a consistent card grid are what let forty routes feel like one product.

**Every hue owns exactly one meaning.** A colour learned on the dashboard means the same thing on the cell scanner. Where a figure has no honest hue — a count, a capacity — it stays neutral rather than being given a decorative one.

Reference language: WiFiman (Ubiquiti) and Firewalla — near-black canvas, saturated data strokes, coloured numerals, thin quality bars, outline metadata tags. Structural reference: the grouped-card, consistent-shape page from macOS System Settings and the Apple pro-app inspectors. Not a consumer router app, not a generic SaaS dashboard, not a terminal utility. Both themes are first-class and each is authored; neither is a desaturated copy of the other.
keyCharacteristics: OKLCH only, and every token is inside sRGB by construction — chroma floored to 98.5% of the in-gamut maximum for its lightness and hue, so declared equals shipped.
Colour lives on INK first, FILL second, and CONTAINER only for the functional roles. Choosing the wrong layer is the standard failure.
Neutrals are tinted toward hue 258 at chroma <= 0.012; `#000` and `#fff` never appear as literals.
Three axes of hue that are not health: identity (which radio), direction (which way the bytes go), spatial (how many antennas). None of them ever acts or means healthy.
Measured signal quality is a five-stop ramp on numerals and bars — a lightness staircase, never a hue wheel, and never routed through the status roles.
Two chip forms, compiler-enforced: a filled Badge for state, an outline Tag for identity and metadata. `BadgeVariant` contains no identity member.
Rethink Sans is the interface voice; JetBrains Mono is the machine voice. There is no third. Material Symbols is an icon font, not a voice.
Depth is tonal. Shadows exist, are optional, and are never load-bearing — in near-black dark mode a shadow has nothing to cast against.
Motion is expressive in curve and duration, capped at `emphasized` (800ms), and never overshoots. One number, 1.03, is the sole sanctioned exception.
Responsive behavior is driven by container queries, not viewport breakpoints.
No runtime asset fetches. Fonts and the icon font are self-hosted and subset at build time — the modem may have no internet.
Build on shadcn/ui first, restyled with these tokens at the call site. Build custom only where shadcn has no answer.

rules.name: The Data-Ink Rule
rules.body: Colour belongs to the reading, not to the container holding it. A card is neutral; the numeral, stroke, bar and glyph disc on it are coloured. Before tinting a surface, ask what fact the tint encodes — if the answer is 'it looked plain', the surface stays neutral. Large tinted blocks are reserved for the functional roles, where the tint IS the state.

rules.name: The Three-Layer Rule
rules.body: Ink (`--X-on-surface`) for values and strokes on neutral ground; fill (`--X` + `--X-foreground`) for compact emphasis; container (`--X-container` + `--on-X-container`) for functional-role blocks only. Identity and direction have no container job. Never cross a pair — a fill takes its own `-foreground`, a container takes its own `on-` ink, and a neutral-ramp ink on a tinted surface is always a bug.

rules.name: The In-Gamut Rule
rules.body: Every token is inside sRGB by construction. This is correctness, not polish: Lightning CSS gamut-maps out-of-range `oklch()` at build time and its mapping is not naive clipping, so an out-of-gamut token ships a colour nobody authored and any separation measured from the source value is fiction. The previous palette had 87 such tokens; this one has zero. Check a new value for gamut before checking it for anything else.

rules.name: The Measured-Separation Rule
rules.body: Colour decisions are measured, never reasoned from hue arithmetic. This replaces the old 40-Degree Rule, which was a proxy for a measurement and behaved like one — it permitted pairs that collapsed and forbade pairs that were fine. Simulate deuteranopia and protanopia, compute OKLab dE, and hold the 0.05 floor on the layer the colour will actually ship on. Degrees of hue separation are not evidence.

rules.name: The Identity-Never-Acts Rule
rules.body: `nr` and `lte` say which radio. They never mean healthy, never tint a control, and never appear in a quality scale. Where a surface carries identity AND reports quality, the quality is encoded non-chromatically — the signal cards use the Material glyph's bar count.

rules.name: The Info-Is-Brand Rule
rules.body: An informational state resolves to the brand ramp; it does not get its own hue. An info chip and a primary button differ by shape and glyph, not by owning two different blues. `--info` is byte-identical to `--primary` in both themes.

rules.name: The Direction-Is-Not-A-Radio Rule
rules.body: Rose and cyan say which way the bytes are going, on either radio. A download figure on the LTE leg is rose-on-violet and neither hue is guessing about the other. Neither carries a second meaning: counts and capacities are neutral. The previous system's cyan meant 'upload and counts', so a carrier-count tile wore upload cyan while reporting nothing about upload.

rules.name: The Glyph-Carries-The-State Rule
rules.body: Colour is never the sole carrier. Every status chip has a glyph, no two states in one slot share a glyph, every directional readout pairs its hue with an arrow, and the quality ramp always pairs its colour with bar length. Load-bearing rather than decorative: adjacent ramp stops are intentionally below the separation floor, and the bar is what makes that safe.

rules.name: The Explicit-Tone Rule
rules.body: Layered translucency is banned for stacked shapes. Concentric rings, halo discs and nested tonal surfaces use the explicit `--tone-{role}-{1,2,3}` steps, because an alpha is a request to whatever happens to be behind it rather than to the token — the same shape compounds to a different colour over a card than over a dialog or a popover. The same reasoning is why dark-mode strokes are solid values rather than `oklch(1 0 0 / 10%)`.

rules.name: The Neutral-Default Rule
rules.body: A figure with no honest hue stays neutral. Adding a colour because a block looked plain is the failure mode this whole system exists to prevent, and it is the one that recurs.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Rethink Sans is the interface, JetBrains Mono is the machine. There is no third typeface. Pairing Rethink Sans with another UI sans (Inter, Geist Sans, IBM Plex, Roboto, Manrope) is forbidden. An icon font is not a voice and does not count.

rules.name: The Machine-Voice Rule
rules.body: `font-mono` is scoped to machine truth that is not itself a changing figure: identifiers (band, EARFCN, PCI, ICCID, IMEI, MAC/IP), static facts read back from config, raw AT responses, log lines, copyable commands. A human-authored label never wears it. The tell: does the value change while the user watches without them acting? Then `font-sans` with `tabular-nums`. Does it hold steady until something reconfigures it? Then `font-mono`.

rules.name: The Weight-Discipline Rule
rules.body: 400 body, 500 labels and medium emphasis, 600 headings and numerics, 700 page titles only.

rules.name: The Tabular-Number Rule
rules.body: Any figure that can change while on screen is `tabular-nums`, in whichever voice it is already in. The class controls digit-width jitter; it does not decide which voice owns the value. A latency readout whose digits shift width reads as the layout twitching, not as the value moving.

rules.name: The Truncation-Pair Rule
rules.body: Where two cards sit side by side as a pair, every text node in their headers carries `min-w-0` and `truncate`. One card wrapping to two lines while its sibling stays at one breaks the paired baseline. Italian is the locale that trips it.

rules.name: The Consistent-Layout Rule
rules.body: Page header (display title plus a muted one-line description, optional pill actions right-aligned) plus a uniform grid of self-contained cards, on every feature page. A bespoke hero-driven layout invented for a single screen is a consistency failure even when it looks good in isolation. A genuine glance surface may earn a hero card; it is a rare exception, never the default.

rules.name: The Card-Wrapped Surface Rule
rules.body: The unit of composition is the card that wraps a settings group, not the page. The card owns its whole content; the page only arranges cards. A feature that scatters loose fragments across the viewport has skipped the card.

rules.name: The Container-Query Rule
rules.body: New responsive behavior is a container query against `@container/main` or a card-local `@container/card`. Reach for a viewport breakpoint only for the page gutter (`px-4 lg:px-6`) or the shell itself. Mixing viewport `sm:` with container `@sm/card:` inside one card breaks on tablets and expanded sidebars.

rules.name: The Cadence-Not-Symmetry Rule
rules.body: Split a page by cadence — what moves every poll above what moves on handover — not by symmetry, and let each card size to its own content. Radio Information was once a symmetric 2-up with both cards `h-full`-locked to each other; the lock forced a static reference card and a live telemetry card to one height, stranding ~200px of dead space in whichever had less to say, and which one that was flipped with the carrier count.

rules.name: The Tonal-Elevation Rule
rules.body: Two surfaces at different conceptual elevations differ by at least one container step. If two surfaces are only distinguishable by their shadow, one of them is on the wrong step of the ramp. This system has no colour to spare for chrome, and in near-black dark mode a shadow is invisible against the ground — a shadow-separated layout has no dark theme at all.

rules.name: The No-Hairline-On-Fill Rule
rules.body: A tonal container never also carries a border. Cards ship `border-0` explicitly, because a hairline over a fill reads as chrome around the colour rather than as the edge of a block. The outline tag is the one deliberate exception in the system: there the border IS the component, because there is no fill for it to sit on top of. `--outline` / `--border` are otherwise for input strokes and genuine table rules only.

rules.name: The Highlight-by-Container Rule
rules.body: Emphasis promotes a surface one container step and changes its ink, rather than adding a translucent wash over a neutral card. A recommended alignment slot becomes a `primary-container` block; a running pipeline step becomes a `primary-container` row.

rules.name: The Radius-Follows-Size Rule
rules.body: A surface's radius is a function of its size and role, not of taste. A 28px tile never sits inside a 20px field, and a banner never out-rounds the card it sits on.

rules.name: The Fill-Over-Stroke Rule
rules.body: When a shape needs to be distinguished from its neighbour, change its fill, not its border. The outline tag is the sanctioned exception, and it is a COMPONENT, not a technique to generalise.

rules.name: The Role-Radius Rule
rules.body: New work uses the role scale (`rounded-inline/field/tile/card/hero/pill`). The legacy `rounded-{sm,md,lg,xl}` chain off `--radius: 0.65rem` still resolves for unconverted call sites — and inside the shadcn primitives themselves — but it is never the correct choice in a new component.

rules.name: The Motion-Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Nothing exceeds `emphasized` (800ms), and `emphasized` is the ceiling, not a starting point. State the rule as the token, never as the number — the number moved once already and every place it had been written out longhand had to be hunted down.

rules.name: The One-Scale Rule
rules.body: A duration in a component is a bug. Every transition reads `duration-[var(--duration-standard)]` (or `-quick` / `-emphasized`) in a className, or `DUR.standard` in a `motion/react` transition; a bare `duration-200`, an inline `{ duration: 0.25 }`, or a `transition-all` with no duration (silently inheriting Tailwind's 150ms) is off the scale and will not retune with it. The exceptions are narrow and each carries a comment: continuous loops with their own tempo, and linear data-driven progress bars. `{ duration: 0 }` as a reduced-motion escape is always fine.

rules.name: The Non-Load-Bearing Rule
rules.body: If a transition never runs — reduced motion, a backgrounded tab, a paint that beat the animation — the UI must already be correct. Every entrance keyframe in `globals.css` is written open-ended (`from` with no `to`): the resting value is the truth and the keyframe only describes the journey. A `requestAnimationFrame`-armed state flip breaks this rule, because rAF does not fire in a background tab.

rules.name: The Transform-Only Rule
rules.body: Animate `transform` and `opacity`. The single sanctioned `width` animation is the carrier-aggregation segment, where the width IS the data and a `scaleX` would distort the band labels riding inside it. The quality meter is the narrow, documented second case: its ENTRANCE is `scaleX`, but its value retarget is layout `width`, because a transform scales the border-radius too and squashed the fill's pill cap into a near-flat ellipse at low percentages — and width changes only on a poll retarget, not per frame.

rules.name: The One-Loop Rule
rules.body: At most one ambient loop per surface, and only where something is genuinely live. Two exist product-wide: the service-ring pulse and the live-ping dot.

rules.name: The No-Overshoot Rule
rules.body: Never springy, never elastic, never rubber-banding. The one sanctioned overshoot is the save-confirmation check at 1.03 scale — and it is a NUMBER, not a sentence: `SAVE_CHECK_OVERSHOOT` / `SAVE_CHECK_KEYFRAMES` / `transitionSaveCheck` in `lib/motion.ts`. A ceiling enforced only by prose is not a ceiling: this rule once cited the save check as the sanctioned exception while the button underneath ran an underdamped spring whose peak was bounded by nothing.

rules.name: The Enter-Only Rule
rules.body: Conditions and navigation have no exit animation. A banner leaving means the condition cleared and that should feel immediate; an outgoing route is already gone, and animating it out only delays the incoming one.

rules.name: The Modal-Exit Rule
rules.body: A modal's exit duration is an INPUT-LATENCY BUDGET, not a taste call, and every modal surface writes its two directions separately: `data-[state=open]:` on `emphasized`, `data-[state=closed]:` on `quick`. Never one unqualified `duration-*` for both. Radix pins `pointer-events: none` on `<body>` for as long as a modal layer is mounted and `<Presence>` holds it mounted until `animationend`, so the entire page is click-dead for exactly the length of the exit animation. The scrim shares the content's clock in both directions, and `quick` is the ceiling for a modal exit — distance does not buy budget: a sheet travels a full viewport edge and still exits on `quick`.

rules.name: The Animations-Preference Rule
rules.body: The reduced-motion switch has THREE states, not two: System (no attribute, `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"`), Full (`data-motion="full"`, `"never"`), Reduced (`data-motion="reduced"`, `"always"`). The absence of the attribute is load-bearing — 'System' removes it rather than writing `data-motion="system"`, and that absence is what lets the bare media query decide. Tailwind's stock `motion-reduce:` compiles to a bare media query with no selector hook, so BOTH `motion-reduce` and `motion-safe` are redefined as `@custom-variant`s in `globals.css`. Redefine both or neither: without the `motion-safe` half, a user on OS-reduce who explicitly picks Full gets every spinner frozen.

rules.name: The Two-Form Rule
rules.body: Status is a filled chip with a glyph. Identity and metadata are an outline tag. Neither form ever does the other's job, and a component that needs both renders both. This is now compiler-enforced: `nr` / `lte` / `spatial` / `downlink` / `uplink` were deleted from `badge.tsx`, so `BadgeVariant` contains no identity member and `variant="nr"` on a Badge fails the build. The deletion fixed two concrete defects — `nr` was a byte-identical class string to `info`, and in light mode 8 of 10 identity-container pairs collapse under simulation.

rules.name: The Every-Chip-Has-A-Glyph Rule
rules.body: Status containers are close by construction — the functional roles share a narrow tint band, and `success-container` against `warning-container` has measured as low as 1.03:1, the same surface to the eye and identical under deuteranopia. The glyph is what separates healthy from degraded. Two states in the same slot must never share a glyph either: `poor` and `bad` both key onto `destructive` and are separated by `signal_cellular_1_bar` vs `signal_cellular_0_bar`.

rules.name: The Identity-Chip Rule
rules.body: Where a surface carries identity AND reports quality, the quality is encoded non-chromatically. On the signal cards that channel is the Material glyph's bar count (the `signal_cellular_{0..4}_bar` family, never the `alt` family, whose 1-bar mark is a 2x4px speck and which has no 0-bar member at all); on a metric row it is the quality bar's length.

rules.name: The Glyph-Disc Rule
rules.body: A state or category icon sits in a filled circle on the role's STRONG fill, never on the pale container. In light mode the identity containers collapse under simulation and the fills do not, so the disc is the only place identity colour is reliably legible — and the disc is what survives when a container fill washes out in sunlight.

rules.name: The One-Quality-Map Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one quality->display map and re-forking it is the failure mode. `components/cellular/signal-quality-display.ts` owns `QUALITY_GLYPH`, `qualityBadgeVariant()`, `qualityMeterTone()` and `qualityInkClass()`. Four rival copies used to exist and were deleted, not merely aligned; one had already drifted, sending `none` through a `default:` arm to `success` so an antenna with NO READING painted green. That is why `qualityMeterTone()` returns `null` rather than a colour for `none` — the absence is a value the caller must handle, not a case it can fall through. `cell-scanner/**` keeps a deliberately separate 3-tier scale (a scan row compares candidate cells to each other; a serving-cell readout compares one cell to physics) and must NOT be unified with it.

rules.name: The Ramp-Needs-A-Bar Rule
rules.body: Ramp ink on a numeral with no bar beside it is a bug, and so is a ramp tone on a fill whose length does not encode the value. Length is the primary encoding and colour is the reinforcement, which is the whole reason adjacent stops are allowed below the separation floor. A missing reading is an empty track (`MetricBar value={null}`, which omits the fill element entirely), never a zero-length fill: an unused antenna drawn as an empty red bar labelled '-140 dBm' reads as a signal problem the user should go and fix.

rules.name: The Skeleton-Mirror Rule
rules.body: A skeleton mirrors the loaded geometry by importing the same shape constant (`TILE_SHAPE`), never by restating numbers, and sizes to the loaded element's LINE BOX rather than its font size. A `min-h-` is not a mirror: measured live, tiles resolved to 118 / 98 / 95px against a 92px floor-based skeleton. The handoff is a pure crossfade on `quick` with the outgoing skeleton overlaid on top of real content, so the card is sized by its content from the first frame and the crossfade contributes zero layout shift.

rules.name: The Loader-and-Dots Rule
rules.body: Step or sample progress is a `Loader2Icon` spinner plus dot indicators. Fill and progress bars are reserved for data visualization — signal strength, quality meters, bandwidth share.

rules.name: The Age-Gated Tone Rule
rules.body: On a surface listing history, two independent axes decide how a row is drawn. TONE is what kind of thing happened; it is a fact about the event, never expires, and is carried by a filled icon disc in the solid role colour for as long as the row exists. WEIGHT is how much the row still deserves attention, and it does expire: a row keeps its tonal container while it is fresh (one hour) or unresolved, then settles onto `surface-container` with its disc at full strength. The disc never consults the age gate. Note that `severity: "info"` here means routine, not good.

rules.name: The Dismiss-Only-Notices Rule
rules.body: A banner gets an X only when it is a notification. A standing condition has no dismiss, because dismissing it would hide a fact that is still true.

rules.name: The State-Honesty Rule
rules.body: A status surface reports what is actually running — saved settings, live service state — never the half-edited form. A control that cannot currently work explains why instead of sitting there dead. A test only runs against saved config. An ambient animation only loops where something is genuinely live: only `searching` spins, because a spinner on a standing condition advertises work that is not happening.

rules.name: The Released-Thing Rule
rules.body: Do not distinguish two states by tone alone when one of them is a released, disabled or absent thing. Measured, `lte-container` and `surface-container-high` were IDENTICAL under deuteranopia — 0.0000 separation — so a dropped carrier and a live LTE carrier were one swatch. The distinction is carried by a glyph or a strikethrough, with tone as reinforcement, and a released carrier stays visible and explicitly marked rather than silently disappearing.

rules.name: The No-Dot-Separator Rule
rules.body: A meta line joining two or more short facts (`PCI 135`, `EARFCN 9485`) uses plain spacing, never a middle-dot glue character — dots read as sloppy filler, not structure. Give the facts room instead of punctuating between them.

rules.name: The Three-State Rule
rules.body: Every data surface ships loading, empty and error — never a blank panel. Non-registered modes REPLACE the body rather than render it empty: a 40px-radius container in the condition's tone, a 56px filled disc, a headline, a description, and an optional retry pill drawn from the container's own ink at 10-15% (never a white wash, which is invisible on a light container). Tone is chosen per condition: no-SIM is `warning`, no-service is `destructive`, searching is `info`, unknown is neutral.

dos: Do put the colour on the reading — the numeral, the stroke, the bar, the disc — and leave the card neutral.
Do pick a LAYER before a colour: ink for values on neutral ground, fill for compact emphasis, container for a functional-role block.
Do pick a PAIR — a fill with its own `-foreground`, or a container with its own `on-` ink.
Do give every status chip a glyph, and give two states in the same slot two different glyphs.
Do use an outline tag for identity and metadata, and a filled chip for state.
Do pair the quality ramp with bar length, always, and add an `sr-only` quality word beside a tinted figure.
Do measure a new colour — gamut first, then contrast, then deuteranopia and protanopia against the layer it will ship on.
Do route every quality->display decision through `components/cellular/signal-quality-display.ts`.
Do reach for the role radii (`rounded-tile` / `card` / `hero` / `pill`) in new work.
Do ship `border-0` on a card and let the tone step carry the separation.
Do write responsive behavior as a container query against `@container/main`.
Do wrap a settings group in a card and let the page arrange cards.
Do put `min-w-0 truncate` on every text node in a paired card's header.
Do mark every changing figure `tabular-nums` in `font-sans`, and reserve `font-mono` for identifiers and raw machine strings.
Do mirror a skeleton's geometry from the same exported shape constant the loaded view uses, and pin heights rather than flooring them.
Do build the loading, empty and error state in the same change as the loaded one.
Do pass `size` explicitly at every `MaterialSymbol` call site.
Do keep interactive targets at 44px on coarse pointers, and let toolbars wrap.
Do make a status surface report SAVED state, and make an incapable control explain itself.
Do defer anything that reboots the modem behind a dialog plus a persistent banner.
Do key every new user-visible string across all five locales; `bun run i18n:check` gates it.
donts: Don't tint a large surface because it looked plain — that is the failure this system exists to prevent.
Don't give identity or direction a large container block; they are ink, outline and disc only.
Don't put ink from one role on another role's surface, or a neutral-ramp ink on a tinted one.
Don't hardcode `text-white` on a destructive fill — in dark mode that fill is LIGHT.
Don't compensate for a mismatched pair with an alpha (`bg-destructive/60`); fix the pair.
Don't use an outline tag as a status indicator, or a filled chip as an identity label.
Don't use `nr` or `lte` to mean 'healthy', or put an identity hue anywhere in a quality scale.
Don't 'level' the quality ramp to satisfy a contrast rule — adjacent stops are below the CVD floor by design and bar length is what carries them.
Don't ship an out-of-gamut `oklch()` — the build will map it and you will not have authored what ships.
Don't argue a colour decision from degrees of hue separation; measure it.
Don't use the numbered `--chart-1..6`; they do not theme.
Don't stack alpha to build concentric shapes — use the explicit `--tone-{role}-{1,2,3}` steps.
Don't put a border on a tonal container, or use `--border` as a card edge.
Don't distinguish two states by tone alone when one of them is a released, disabled or absent thing.
Don't animate `width` (the aggregation segment is the sole exception; the meter's documented retarget is the one narrow second case) or exceed `emphasized`.
Don't write a raw duration (`duration-200`, `{ duration: 0.25 }`) or a `transition-all` with no duration.
Don't add a third entrance stagger step, a fifth duration, or a spring.
Don't add an exit animation to a banner or a route transition.
Don't give a modal one unqualified `duration-*` for both directions, or leave its scrim without one.
Don't loop an animation where nothing is genuinely live.
Don't put an icon in a `CardHeader`.
Don't invent a bespoke hero-driven layout for one screen.
Don't mix Material Symbols and lucide inside a single route.
Don't introduce a third typeface, or set a human-authored label in mono.
Don't reach for 13px outside a dense metric row, or for the pre-auth scale outside `/` and `/login/`.
